title: What People Really Think
briefing: The first risk culture survey is back. Managers rate culture highly; front-line staff do not. A comment says: 'Raise a problem here and you become the problem.'
The CEO wants the results 'positioned carefully'.

context.text: Near-miss reporting, which you fixed years ago, is still one of the healthiest signals in the business.
The depot expenses fraud was known to two colleagues who said nothing. This survey is partly why.

evidence.title: Survey results
evidence.body: 'I can raise concerns without fear': managers 81% agree, front line 38%. 'Bad news travels up quickly': managers 74%, front line 29%. Response rate 64%.

evidence.title: Selected comments
evidence.body: 'Raise a problem here and you become the problem.' 'Targets matter more than how you hit them.' 'My manager listens, his manager doesn't.'

evidence.title: Speak-up line data
evidence.body: 4 reports in 12 months across 1,240 staff. Benchmark for similar firms: 15-25.

questions.prompt: What is the most important finding?

options.label: The 40-point gap between managers and front line: leaders believe people speak up; people don't
options.feedback: The gap is the risk: leadership is blind to what the front line knows.

options.label: Managers' high scores show a strong culture
options.feedback: Self-assessment by those in charge is not the culture of those reporting to them.

questions.prompt: What does 4 speak-up reports a year suggest?

options.label: Under-use: well below the 15-25 benchmark, consistent with fear of raising concerns
options.feedback: Low reports read with the survey suggest silence, not a lack of issues.

options.label: The phone line is broken
options.feedback: Check it, but the survey explains it better.

questions.prompt: How do you respond to 'position it carefully'?

options.label: Present the results in full with context and a plan; careful framing, not careful omission
Report the managers' scores as 'overall culture'

schedules.description: A driver goes to the regulator and the press about fatigue rules being ignored at one depot

options.label: Hold the results until next year's survey confirms them

schedules.description: A driver goes to the regulator and the press about fatigue rules being ignored at one depot

questions.prompt: Which action plan do you propose?

options.label: Senior leaders hold listening sessions at sites, act visibly on three issues raised, protect and thank people who speak up, and re-survey in 12 months
options.feedback: Culture changes when people see leaders act on what they hear.

options.label: A poster campaign about speaking up
options.feedback: Words without changed behaviour reinforce cynicism.

options.label: Mandatory e-learning for all staff
options.feedback: Puts the burden on the people who are afraid, not on those who create the fear.

questions.prompt: How will you know it's working?

options.label: Speak-up reports rising toward benchmark, near-miss reports holding, the manager/front-line gap narrowing in the re-survey
options.feedback: Several signals, including ones that should rise.

options.label: Fewer speak-up reports
options.feedback: In this situation, more reports is the sign of success.

options.label: The CEO feels the culture has improved
options.feedback: The original problem was leaders' perception.

lesson: Culture risk shows in the gap between how leaders and the front line see the organisation. Share uncomfortable results honestly and let people see leaders act.
